notes: Example built from the source rule (week 10, year 14). Current Carrier/Bryant/Payne style: week then 2-digit year, then a plant letter. Same rule on https://inspectorhandbook.com/hvac/bryant. Era start not published; 1990 assumed because the YYMM style below is documented as 1980s
Example built from the source rule. Legacy 1980s style: 2-digit year then 2-digit month
Leading letter is ignored; positions 2-3 year, 4-5 week. Heil page gives the same current format and says the H-prefixed style was 1980-1989: https://inspectorhandbook.com/hvac/heil
First two digits ignored, next two are the year, fifth character is a month letter. Month letters skip I, as in the Lennox table. Era start not published; 1990 assumed
First two digits are the plant code, 3-4 the year, 5th a month letter (A Jan to M Dec, no I). Month key also on https://inspectorhandbook.com/hvac/lennox
Style 1 from 2010: 2-digit year then 2-digit week. Plate usually also prints MFR date
Style 1 from 2002 to 2009: 1-digit year then 2-digit week
HVAC style 1: plant letter, week, 2-digit year. Same shape as an ICP serial but the digit order is reversed, so the brand must be right. Era start not published; 1990 assumed
HVAC styles 2-4: a middle factory letter (F, M, G, W or N), then week and 2-digit year
Water heater styles 1, 2, 4, 5: letter prefix (R, RH, RHLN, RHNG, RU), then month and 2-digit year. Some Rheem heaters put the week here instead (next row); the plate usually prints the date
Water heater styles 3 and 7: letter prefix (may include a factory letter), then week and 2-digit year
Tankless style 6: year then month separated by a period
10-digit serial: 2-digit year then month. Amana uses the same current style: https://inspectorhandbook.com/hvac/amana. Era start not published; 2000 assumed
Style 2: four prefix letters, then year and month. Also Option 1 on https://inspectorhandbook.com/hvac/daikin
Style 10: Goodman-built Daikin units use the Goodman year-month style
Since 2004: plant letter, year tens digit, month letter, year units digit. Month letters A-M without I (J = September on https://inspectorhandbook.com/hvac/luxaire)

Pre-2004 style: ignored letter, month letter (skips J), year letter (A to N repeat for 1992-2004). Tables transcribed from the Luxaire page; the York page on building-center.org shows the same layout but its charts are images
Styles 1a-1c: optional letter, 2-digit year, then week (week since 2008). Same rule on https://inspectorhandbook.com/water-heaters/aosmith
Example built from the source rule. Before 2008 the two digits after the year are the month
Style 4 (discontinued 2008-2010): month letter then 2-digit year
Styles 2-3 (discontinued): first letter ignored, second letter is the month, then 2-digit year

Year letter repeats every 20 years, so every serial has two or three candidate years. Use the ANSI Z21.10 revision year on the plate or other evidence to pick. Tankless Bradford White units made by Rinnai use the Rinnai style
Since 2009: year letter then month letter
Before 2009: year then month separated by a period
1999-2008 style 3: year then month with no separator
Five model characters, 2-digit year, month code (1-9, then X, Y, Z for Oct-Dec), day of month. building-center.org has a Navien page but its content is members-only
Older hyphenated style with a full YYYYMMDD date block
Style 2 (2011-2022): month, day, 2-digit year, then a letter and sequence. The 1994-2011 letter style is not encoded because its letter tables are images
Style 2a: 16 digits; ignore the first two
Style 3 (since Sep 2021): always 21 characters; characters 10-11 year, 12-14 day of year

First letter is the last digit of the year (C = 2013), last letter the month (B = February). The source gives only one worked example; the rest of both letter tables is extrapolated, so treat anything but C and B as unverified
First digit is the last digit of the year only, so the decade is ambiguous. Inspector blog, not manufacturer literature
No published serial date code found. The date has to come from the cabinet data label or from True with the serial number
No published serial date code found. Machines are leased; Auto-Chlor service records hold the install date
No serial date code. The data plate carries a job number and a printed date (MM/DD/YYYY), per the building-center.org summary (full page is members-only)
